evals.prompt: We closed Northwind Logistics three months ago, $480k ARR, renews 1 Feb 2027 with a 90-day notice period. The AE's handover says they want to 'improve reporting and drive adoption across claims'. Build me the mutual success plan.
evals.expected_output: A full plan in New-plan mode: the handover language rejected as product wishes and climbed to business objectives, 3-5 objectives with unbroken outcome chains, baselines with sources and as-of dates or a declared proxy tier, SMART goals with owners on both sides, milestones with time-to-value first, a risk register over all eleven categories, RAG thresholds as numbers, an Assumptions table, a Coverage Ledger over the seven families, and a customer-facing copy block below the divider.
assertions: Computes and prints the opt-out deadline as 2026-11-03 (renewal_date minus 90 days) and uses it as the planning anchor rather than the renewal date
Refuses 'improve reporting' and 'drive adoption' as objectives and climbs each to a business objective with a candidate metric, marking them Proposed until the customer confirms
C18 — the Baseline Orders section (§3A) appears in the output before the SMART Goals section (§3B); no goal appears above the orders
C18 — every row in §3B carries a baseline with all three of value, source and as-of date; a row missing any one of the three is not present in §3B

C18 — every objective whose baseline is incomplete appears in §3A with a metric definition, a source system and field, a named customer person who will measure it, and a pull-by date, and no SMART goal, target value or target date is written for that objective anywhere in the output
No cell in §3A reads 'TBC', 'n/a', 'the team', or a role with no person's name attached
Every objective names one customer owner and one vendor owner as people, never a team, and the plan prints the share of milestones carrying a customer-side owner against the 40% gate
Includes a leading indicator per goal that moves within 30 days, with its threshold stated
Ends with an Assumptions table where each row states a concrete consequence, and a Coverage Ledger over all seven signal families with a stated confidence cap
Emits the customer version inside a fenced text block below the divider with no unfilled placeholders and no ARR, health, risk or forecast language

evals.prompt: Here's our success plan for Acme. Objectives are: 1) increase adoption, 2) roll out to more teams, 3) get executive buy-in. Owners are 'CSM' and 'Acme team'. Is this any good?
evals.expected_output: Rewrite mode: a gate audit of all three objectives against Specific/Measurable/Assignable/Realistic/Time-bound plus the compensation, ownership, money and 30-day tests, each rewritten into a SMART goal with the missing inputs marked UNKNOWN rather than invented, and a short list of what must be renegotiated with the customer.
assertions: Audits each existing objective against the gate and states which letters and tests it fails, rather than simply rewriting silently
Rewrites all three, and the rewrite of 'get executive buy-in' becomes a named sponsor plus a signed charter with a date
Flags that 'CSM' and 'Acme team' are not owners and requires named humans on both sides
C18 — because no baseline exists for any of the three objectives, the output writes no SMART goal, no target value and no target date for them; each becomes a §3A Baseline Order row instead

C18 — each Baseline Order names the metric definition, the source system and field, the customer person who will measure it and the date they will pull it by; where the customer measurer is unknown it is escalated to the executive sponsor as a decision rather than assigned to us
Does not substitute an industry benchmark, a plausible number, or a target with the baseline left blank
States that objectives inherited from a handover or written by us start at Proposed and cannot be reported as plan content until the customer agrees objective, baseline, success criteria and timeline
Produces a short list of what has to be renegotiated with the customer, each item with an owner and a date

evals.prompt: Acme's VP Ops who signed off our success plan left last month. Their replacement starts Monday. What do we do with the plan?
evals.expected_output: Re-baseline mode: affected objectives dropped to Proposed, the rule that inherited acceptance is not acceptance, a 30-minute re-discovery agenda built from the original business case, the effect on the renewal evidence timeline measured against the opt-out deadline, and the risk-register and status changes that follow.
assertions: Drops the affected objectives to Proposed and states explicitly that inherited acceptance is not acceptance
Produces a re-discovery agenda that quotes the predecessor's objectives with dates and asks which of them are still the new sponsor's
Asks what the new sponsor is measured on, and treats an objective nobody is graded on as not ready
Ties the timing to the opt-out deadline rather than the renewal date, and checks whether any objective can still be Verified before it
Sends the executive-level outreach from a VP rather than the CSM, with a date
Does not claim the account will churn or state a probability, and keeps risk language out of anything the customer would read
C18 — any objective whose baseline definition or measurement owner left with the departing sponsor is returned to §3A as a Baseline Order rather than carried forward with the predecessor's number

evals.prompt: Quarterly review for Northwind next week. Attached is the plan JSON. Which objectives are actually on track and what do I need a decision on?
evals.expected_output: Review mode: deterministic attainment and schedule variance per objective from scripts/plan_health.py, derived RAG statuses with the threshold that decided each one, the unmeasured guard applied, the flags for Delivered-not-Verified and zero-Verified-before-opt-out, and a decisions list with owners and dates.
assertions: Runs or reproduces scripts/plan_health.py and shows attainment, elapsed and schedule variance in percentage points per objective
C18 — prints the baseline gate before the objective table: how many of the 4 objectives carry value, source and as-of date, the count of Baseline Orders outstanding and the earliest pull-by date
C18 — reports O4 as Watchpoint with the reason naming the missing baseline fields, and writes no attainment, target or RAG-on-progress claim for it
C18 — prints the tier label for O2's attested baseline ([T3 ... stated, not measured]) and states that the label travels with every figure derived from it, including anything the customer reads
Derives each RAG status from the stated thresholds and prints the reason that decided it, rather than asserting a status
Treats an objective whose leading indicator has never been measured as Watchpoint rather than On Track
Flags any objective at Delivered but never Verified as not reportable as achieved
Flags zero Verified objectives inside 120 days of the opt-out deadline as a value-evidence gap with an owner and a date
Every decision carries a named decision-maker, a date, and what is blocked until then
States confidence no higher than the Coverage Ledger permits and names the blind spots

evals.prompt: Our sponsor at Meridian wants a goal in the plan saying we'll cut their onboarding time by 40% this year. Nobody has ever measured how long onboarding takes today and their ops lead says pulling it would be a pain. Just put the 40% in and we'll baseline it later.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to write the goal. The output states what must be measured, out of which system, by which named person on the customer side and by when, as a Baseline Order; it offers the four proxy methods in order of defensibility with the evidentiary label each carries; and it says plainly why a target written before its baseline is discounted at renewal. No 40% target appears as a plan goal.
assertions: C18 — refuses to write the goal: no target value, no target date and no SMART goal statement for the 40% reduction appears anywhere in the output
C18 — emits a Baseline Order instead, naming the metric definition with population and exclusions, the source system and field, the named customer person who will pull it, and a pull-by date

Treats 'we'll baseline it later' as the failure mode by name and states the consequence: a starting point reconstructed after the target was set is discounted by the customer's finance team at renewal
Offers the four proxies in order (reconstruct, control group, customer-attested, benchmark x0.5) and attaches the evidentiary label each carries, never describing a proxy as a measurement
States that a tier-4 benchmark figure never appears in the customer-facing block or the renewal value case, and that a tier-3 attested figure names its attester and the date
Where no proxy can be built, converts the objective into 'establish the baseline' with the named customer measurer and the pull-by date as its owner and target date
Does not invent an industry benchmark for onboarding time or state a plausible current value
Names the escalation path when the ops lead will not pull the number: the executive sponsor decides, and our own pull does not substitute for their confirmation
